segments.text: And euery good and faythfull christian man feeleth in hym selfe, bowe he feedeth of Christe, eatyng his fleshe, and drynkyng his bloud. For he putteth the hole hope and trust of his redemption and saluation in that only sacrifice, which Christ made vpon the Crosse, hauyng his body there broken, and his bloud there shedde for the remission of his synnes. And this greate benefite of Christe, the faithfull man earnestly considereth in his mynde, chaweth and digesteth it with the stomake of his harte, spiritually receauynge Christe wholly into hym, and gyuyng agayne hym selfe wholly vnto Christe.
And this is the eatyng of Christes flesh & drinkyng of his blud, the felyng wherof is to euery mā, the felyng how he eateth & drynketh Christ, which none euil mā nor mēbre of the diuel can do
